profiles.summary: Public archive for studying typefaces in real identities, publications, packaging, interfaces, and other artifacts.
limitations: Entries document observed use rather than licensing suitability.
Contributor captions and classifications can vary in depth.
Images and referenced work remain third-party content and must not be redistributed without permission.

notes: Retain source links and creator credits.
Use examples as research evidence, not copying instructions.

evidence.claim: Fonts In Use operates as a public archive of real-world typography with searchable use examples.

profiles.summary: Curated library of fonts presented for commercial-use research, with family-level licence pages and webfont tooling.
limitations: Licence terms vary by family and the linked licence must be read before use.
A catalogue label is not a substitute for legal review of the original licence.
Webfont conversion and redistribution rights differ across licences.

notes: Treat each family licence as authoritative.
Do not persist font binaries in Tessli.

evidence.claim: Font Squirrel presents hand-picked fonts for commercial-use discovery and exposes licence information per family.
Font-family pages distinguish licence and webfont-kit availability, so usage conditions remain family-specific.

profiles.summary: Curated gallery of typefaces available under multiple free-licence models, organized for visual font discovery.
limitations: The collection covers a variety of free licences rather than one uniform usage grant.
The original typeface source and licence must be checked before use.
Coverage and metadata depth vary by typeface.

notes: Link to the original font source where available.
Do not infer commercial rights from the word free alone.

evidence.claim: Free Faces describes itself as a curated collection of typefaces available under a variety of free licences.

profiles.summary: Curated display of open-source typefaces that sends users to original designer or repository pages for official downloads and licences.
limitations: Open Foundry is a display rather than the authoritative download host.
The original project page prevails when licence information conflicts.
Commercial-use permission depends on each font licence.

notes: Follow the original project link for downloads and licence text.
Credit designers and foundries where required or appropriate.

evidence.claim: Open Foundry is a curated platform for open-source fonts and states that official downloads live on the original project pages.

profiles.summary: Font-pairing and brand-kit workspace built around curated Google Fonts and Fontshare combinations.
limitations: Pairings are curated starting points rather than guarantees for a specific brand or language.
Advanced collections and exports require a paid plan.
The underlying font licences still come from Google Fonts or Fontshare.

notes: Review the underlying font licence separately.
Do not treat generated brand-kit output as unique trademark clearance.

evidence.claim: FontPair offers curated font pairings from Google Fonts and Fontshare plus brand-kit exploration.
FontPair documents paid access for expanded pairings, collections, and exports.

profiles.summary: Libre type foundry publishing experimental open-source fonts with use, modification, redistribution, and attribution guidance.
limitations: Licence and attribution details must be checked for the selected family.
Modified versions may require redistribution under the original licence.
Experimental display faces may have limited language coverage or interface suitability.

notes: Credit the type designer and Velvetyne as required.
Retain the original licence when modifying or redistributing a font.

evidence.claim: Velvetyne states that its hosted fonts are libre and open source and may be used, modified, and redistributed under their licence conditions.
Velvetyne documents attribution and same-licence redistribution duties for its fonts.

profiles.summary: Adobe-hosted font library integrated with Creative Cloud for desktop activation and web-project embedding.
limitations: Library access and desktop activation depend on an eligible Adobe account and plan.
Adobe-hosted web fonts must use the provided embed workflow and cannot be self-hosted under the standard service licence.
App embedding, server use, transfer, and packaging can require separate licences from the foundry.

notes: The client or workspace must own the applicable Adobe subscription.
Do not persist or redistribute Adobe font files through Tessli.

evidence.claim: Adobe Fonts provides plan-dependent access to a hosted font library through Creative Cloud accounts.
Adobe web fonts use Adobe-provided embed code and standard service terms do not permit self-hosting the font files.

profiles.summary: Visual and programmatic animation tooling for sequencing HTML/SVG, Three.js, and React Three Fiber scenes.
limitations: The editor and runtime add workflow and state-management complexity beyond simple transitions.
Project state and authored assets require explicit source-control and deployment decisions.
Production accessibility, performance, and reduced-motion behavior remain application responsibilities.

notes: Review package licences and production-state export guidance.
Keep authored project assets within the project repository, not Tessli records.

evidence.claim: Theatre.js documents animation workflows for React Three Fiber, Three.js, and HTML/SVG plus concepts and code APIs.
Theatre.js objects and props can be changed through its UI or code and sequenced in sheets.

profiles.summary: Modular JavaScript animation engine covering animations, timelines, SVG, text, draggable interaction, and WAAPI workflows.
limitations: Complex timelines and effects still require performance and reduced-motion review.
Framework lifecycle integration remains the application author's responsibility.
The broad API can be excessive for simple layout transitions.

notes: Import only the modules required by the project.
Test animation behavior across input modes and visibility changes.

evidence.claim: Anime.js documents modular installation and direct or subpath imports for JavaScript projects.
Anime.js documents animation, timeline, SVG, text, utilities, draggable, and WAAPI feature areas.

profiles.summary: Small automatic-animation utility that adds transitions when direct child elements are added, removed, or moved.
limitations: Automatic transitions offer less sequencing control than timeline libraries.
The parent-child DOM relationship must fit the utility's observation model.
Reduced-motion, layout performance, and complex nested interactions still require product testing.

notes: Use for bounded layout transitions rather than as a complete motion system.
Review the current package licence and framework integration guidance.

evidence.claim: FormKit describes AutoAnimate as a zero-config drop-in utility for smooth transitions in React, Vue, and other JavaScript applications.
